text: When Aunt Em came there to live. <break time="0.8s" /> She was a young, pretty wife. <break time="0.8s" /> But the sun and wind. <break time="0.8s" /> Had changed her, too. <break time="0.8s" /> They had taken the sparkle. <break time="0.8s" /> From her eyes. <break time="0.8s" /> And left them a sober gray. <break time="0.8s" /> She was thin and pale now. <break time="0.8s" /> And she never smiled. <break time="0.8s" /> When Dorothy. <break time="0.8s" /> Who was an orphan. <break time="0.8s" /> First came to her. <break time="0.8s" /> The childs laughter. <break time="0.8s" /> Startled Aunt Em. <break time="0.8s" /> Aunt Em would scream. <break time="0.8s" /> And press her hand on her heart. <break time="0.8s" /> Whenever she heard. <break time="0.8s" /> The girls merry voice. <break time="0.8s" /> She still looked at Dorothy. <break time="0.8s" /> And wondered. <break time="0.8s" /> How the girl could find. <break time="0.8s" /> Anything to laugh at. <break time="0.8s" /> Uncle Henry never laughed. <break time="0.8s" /> For he worked hard. <break time="0.8s" /> From morning till night. <break time="0.8s" /> He was gray. <break time="0.8s" /> From his long beard. <break time="0.8s" /> To his rough boots. <break time="0.8s" /> And he rarely spoke. <break time="0.8s" /> It was Toto. <break time="0.8s" /> That made Dorothy laugh. <break time="0.8s" /> And saved her. <break time="0.8s" /> From growing as gray as everything else. <break time="0.8s" /> Toto was a little black dog. <break time="0.8s" /> With long, silky hair. <break time="0.8s" /> And small black eyes. <break time="0.8s" /> That twinkled merrily. <break time="0.8s" /> Toto played all day long. <break time="0.8s" /> And Dorothy played with him. <break time="0.8s" /> And loved him dearly.
